t: You're at the site of the Palace of Placentia, also known as Greenwich Palace, a royal residence on the south bank of the Thames. Prince Humphrey, Duke of Gloucester, first built it in 1443, and it was designed for pleasure, entertainment and escape from the city. It became a hospital in the 1690s. Its royal story is a Tudor one. Henry VIII was born here, and so were his daughters Mary I and Elizabeth I. His son Edward VI died here in 1553, still a young king ruled through a regency council.
